title: A free beginning without every answer

captions.physics: Trying pleasure without a detailed script
captions.emotions: Feeling open to a new experience

meaning: Spontaneous leisure can stay light when unclear expectations allow an open experiment instead of compulsory certainty about every feeling.
text: The unknown can unsettle and delight at once. The Fool in the physical position of Svadhisthana helps begin something pleasant without a detailed script. The Moon in energy leans towards seeking certainty through guesses about a future impression. The Fool in emotions allows openness to something new to be felt. The first Fool concerns freely experimenting through action; the second concerns its light inward experience. Both benefit from room for this response without knowing beforehand what will happen or how strongly each must enjoy it.

For example, you happen to notice a workshop with an open table for simple stamps. Making a postcard appeals, but doubts arise: will it look attractive, and might the other become bored? **A free beginning allows pleasure without a ready answer.** You can try one print and ask about another. A small actual experiment clarifies more than mentally sorting possible moods. It need not become a whole collection or prove an ideal shared activity for the evening.

The difficulty is discussing possible impressions until the light wish disappears, or agreeing to everything to avoid naming uncertainty. An open trial remains free when stopping is possible. If a postcard is enough for one, the other may continue separately through clear agreement without explaining each mood change or making it shared.
